what_its_for: This cream or gel numbs the skin or gums before minor procedures like blood draws, IV placement, minor skin surgeries, or dental work. It works by temporarily blocking pain signals in the area where it is applied.
how_to_take: This medicine is applied directly to the skin or gums — do NOT swallow it or put it inside your body. For skin: squeeze a thick layer of cream onto the area that needs to be numbed, then cover it with the special clear dressing (plastic wrap) included in the package or as directed by your doctor. Leave it on for the amount of time your doctor recommends (usually 1 to 2 hours before a procedure). For gums: your dentist will apply the gel directly into the space between your teeth and gums using a special applicator. Always wash your hands before and after applying.
dosing: Use only the amount prescribed by your doctor or as directed on the package. For adults and children over 3 months, a small pea-sized to dime-sized amount is usually enough for a small area. Do not apply to a larger area of skin or leave it on longer than instructed, as too much medicine can be absorbed into your body. For infants under 12 months, use only under strict doctor supervision.
missed_dose: Since this medicine is usually used only once before a procedure, a missed dose schedule does not typically apply. If you forget to apply it at the right time before your appointment, contact your doctor or nurse for guidance. Do not apply extra to make up for it.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the tube or package tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the cream if it has changed color or smells different than usual.
what_to_avoid: Do not apply near your eyes, inside the ears, or on open wounds or broken skin unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Do not wrap the treated area too tightly, as this can increase the amount absorbed into your body. Avoid applying to large areas of skin. Do not use on children under 3 months of age without a doctor's direct supervision. Do not eat or drink immediately after a dental gel application until the numbness wears off, to avoid accidentally biting your cheek or tongue.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you notice any of the following after using this medicine: unusual dizziness or lightheadedness, blurred vision, ringing in the ears, feeling confused or agitated, fast or irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing, seizures, pale or bluish skin color (especially around the lips or fingernails in infants, which may be a sign of a rare but serious condition called methemoglobinemia), or severe skin reactions such as burning, swelling, or blistering at the application site. Also tell your doctor if you are allergic to any numbing medicines.
when_it_works: The cream usually starts to numb the skin within 45 to 60 minutes when applied under a covering. Full numbness is generally reached within 1 to 2 hours. The numbing effect lasts about 1 to 2 hours after the covering is removed. The dental gel works within a few minutes when applied by your dentist.
special_populations: Infants and young children: This medicine must be used very carefully in babies, especially those under 12 months old or premature infants, because they are at higher risk for a serious side effect called methemoglobinemia (a condition where the blood cannot carry oxygen properly). Always follow your doctor's exact instructions for children. Pregnant women: It is generally considered safe to use during pregnancy when needed, but always tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding mothers: Small amounts may pass into breast milk, but it is generally considered safe; check with your doctor to be sure. Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may absorb more medicine through the skin and may be more sensitive to side effects.
